ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances put the actual route at 21.5 km against a recommended 20.4 km — a deviation of 1.10 km — and POL-RD-22 sets the tolerance at 1.0 km, so this deviation is outside tolerance and the refund matrix is engaged. Because both recorded distances are present and clean, the deviation is established on the trip record and no POL-GEN-26 escalation arises on this fact.

The driver-device trace independently shows the vehicle leaving the CTE at the Toa Payoh Rise exit, running Thomson Road and then Newton Road, and only rejoining the recommended line at North Bridge Road / Rochor Road. The trace establishes which route was taken and when, under POL-RD-22, and matches the route_deviation_detected and route_rejoined events in the trip record.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The LTA traffic advisory for the CTE segment the driver left (towards City, Toa Payoh Rise to Rochor Road), overlapping the trip window, records advisory type NONE and speed bands 4-5 with no incident, roadwork or closure. POL-RD-23 names only congestion, incident or closure as justifying, and NONE is not one of them, so the driver's asserted 'CTE morning jam' is unsupported by the very data that would verify it.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, or verbally with a call recording as evidence; the chat log is contiguous and carries zero messages, the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty, and no call recording exists. No notice and no rider acknowledgment can be established, so the deviation was not agreed.

On POL-RD-24 the case falls squarely in row (d): not traffic-justified and a deviation over 1 km. The remedy is a refund of the excess distance fare in full, computed without surge as deviation distance times the per-km rate — 1.10 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.79 SGD — rounded to the cent. The rider is therefore owed 0.79 SGD as a PARTIAL_REFUND, and the fare ledger's own derived money block carries the same figure.

I do not overstate the rider's recovery. The rider's claim asks for the whole 34.62 SGD metered fare, but POL-RD-24 provides no row that voides the entire trip fare for a route deviation, and POL-GEN-03 defines PARTIAL_REFUND as the part of the charge that is returned. The record does not support a FULL_REFUND of 34.62 SGD; it supports the excess distance fare of 0.79 SGD, and that is the relief the rider should be granted.

This case is one the AI may decide. The disputed value is 34.62 SGD, which sits in POL-GEN-22's 10.00-50.00 band, neither profile carries a fraud flag (both are 0), and every artifact here is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the ruling stands at the required 0.80 confidence. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied, since route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false, and the deviation of 1.10 km would be within 2 km in any event. There is no open fact requiring POL-GEN-26 escalation.

The rider asks for the whole 34.62 SGD morning fare back, but POL-RD-24 never returns a trip fare: the remedy it provides for a reroute is the excess distance fare alone. The trip was in fact completed to Raffles Hospital, North Bridge Road, and the fare was finalised on the metered distance actually driven (21.5 km) after the driver rejoined the recommended route. The rider's claim to the entire fare is unsupported by the clause that governs it.

Whichever row of POL-RD-24 could conceivably apply on this record, the driver's maximum exposure is the same: rows (b) and (d) both pay the whole excess distance fare and nothing else, and neither touches the base fare, distance fare, time fare, surge (7.32 SGD), ERP or platform fee that make up the 34.62 SGD charged. There is no row of the matrix that returns the trip fare, so the rider's demand for the full fare fails on the clause itself.

The exposure is arithmetically bounded at 0.79 SGD: the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd without surge, 1.10 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.792, rounded to 0.79 SGD. The payments ledger's own derived block returns excess_distance_fare_sgd = 0.79 on the same inputs, so even on the rider's best row the driver retains 33.83 SGD of the 34.62 SGD charged.

The distance truly in issue is 1.10 km, not a route: the deviation distance is measured on the platform's recorded distances under POL-RD-22 - trip_record.actual_distance_km 21.5 minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 20.4 - and the clause expressly forbids re-measuring it from the sparse trace, which records only 18.171 km over 69 fixes. The rider booked a metered ride, and 1.10 km of metered distance is the whole of the contested distance.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record: the LTA advisory for the recommended segment (Central Expressway towards City, Toa Payoh Rise to Rochor Road) records advisory_type NONE across the trip window, with speed bands 4-5 and no incident, roadwork or closure, so POL-RD-23's requirement of congestion, an incident or a closure is not met and the driver's bare assertion of a CTE jam cannot carry it. That still leaves the driver's obligation at the excess distance fare and no more; the deviation itself lasted only from 08:27:08 to 08:35:30, roughly eight minutes, before the driver rejoined at North Bridge Road / Rochor Road.

This is a case the AI decides, not one to hold open: the disputed value is 34.62 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's 10.00-50.00 SGD band, neither profile carries a fraud flag of 1 or more, the record shows no safety indicator, and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false). Every artifact on the file is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no fact POL-GEN-26 names is unestablished and there is nothing for a human reviewer to resolve; the record settles the refund at the excess distance fare.

ruling.explanation:
The rider filed this dispute, and the outcome is read from the rider's claim against the record.

What the record establishes. The platform's recorded distances put the actual route at 21.5 km against a recommended 20.4 km — a deviation of 1.10 km (POL-RD-22) — and the tolerance is 1.0 km, so this deviation is outside tolerance and the refund matrix is engaged. Both recorded distances are present and clean, so the deviation is established on the trip record, not on the sparse trace (which measures only 18.171 km over 69 fixes and is expressly not used to re-measure distance). The driver-device trace confirms which route was taken and when: the vehicle left the CTE at the Toa Payoh Rise exit, ran Thomson Road and then Newton Road, and rejoined at North Bridge Road / Rochor Road, matching the trip record's deviation and rejoin events.

The two mitigating grounds both fail. The LTA traffic advisory for the CTE segment towards City (Toa Payoh Rise to Rochor Road), overlapping the trip window, records advisory type NONE with speed bands 4-5 and no incident, roadwork or closure; POL-RD-23 names only congestion, an incident or a closure as justifying a reroute, so the driver's asserted 'CTE morning jam' is not supported by the data that would verify it. And the driver did not inform the rider: the chat log is contiguous and carries zero messages, the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty, and no call recording exists, so notice under POL-RD-21 cannot be established and the deviation was not agreed.

Money. On POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies, and it is row (d) — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — whose remedy is a refund of the excess distance fare in full. That is deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge: 1.10 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 0.792, rounded to 0.79 SGD, the same figure the fare ledger's derived block carries. The rider asked for the whole 34.62 SGD metered fare, but no row of the matrix returns the trip fare, and the trip was in fact completed to Raffles Hospital with the fare finalised on the 21.5 km actually driven; nothing in the clause touches base fare, distance fare, time fare, the 7.32 SGD surge, the 2.00 SGD ERP or the 0.90 SGD platform fee. So the rider is owed 0.79 SGD of the 34.62 SGD charged, and the driver retains the remaining 33.83 SGD.

Decision and confidence. The disputed value is 34.62 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's 10.00-50.00 SGD band; neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (both 0); no safety indicator appears; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false). POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-22 therefore require confidence of 0.80, and every artifact on this file is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the ruling stands at 0.90. No fact POL-GEN-26 names is left unestablished on these limbs, so no escalation arises. Route deviation carries no referral clause in this version, so there is no referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
